title: Only audience[0] is checked for persona_ requirements, but the token is minted for every requested audience
description:
persona-grpc/src/service.rs:112-117 parses persona_ extension parameters from req.audience[0] only:

    let ext = AudienceExtensions::parse(&req.audience[0])?;

The presence check at service.rs:146 is then made against that single parsed value. But service.rs:176-180 signs the token with the entire list:

    let audiences: Vec<&str> = req.audience.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
    self.signer.sign_jwt_svid(&spiffe_id_str, &audiences, persona_ext)

Trigger: a caller sends audience = ["https://harmless.example", "https://bank.example?persona_require_presence=hardware"].

What goes wrong: only element 0 is parsed, so require_presence resolves to None and the check at line 146 passes trivially. The issued JWT carries aud = both strings. The relying party at bank.example -- which encoded its requirement in its own audience string exactly as SPEC-HIA.md:250 instructs -- receives a token whose aud contains its expected value, validates it (ValidateJWTSVID at service.rs:224 checks only that aud contains the requesting audience), and accepts a credential whose presence requirement was never evaluated. The persona claim in that same token asserts "present": true whenever any enumerated claim reports non-None presence.

The audit log makes this hard to spot after the fact: service.rs:195 logs only audience = %req.audience[0], so the audience that actually mattered never appears in the svid_issued event.

Fix direction: parse every element of req.audience and enforce the strictest requirement across all of them (or reject a request whose elements carry conflicting persona_ parameters). Log the full audience list, not just the first element.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.47 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
